# Corpus slugs whose filming location is public: the round sets committed before
# scoring moved server-side carried lat/lng in web/rounds.json, and this repo is
# public, so those coordinates are recoverable from git history (including the
# pre-squash PR commits GitHub keeps fetchable). Ground truth is clip-level, so
# ANY round cut from one of these clips -- at any moment -- can be looked up
# rather than guessed.
#
# make_rounds.py excludes these from every pool it draws, and check.py refuses a
# set that contains one. The list only ever grows: a slug is here because its
# coordinates escaped, and history does not un-happen. Regenerate the union with:
#
#   for c in $(git log --all --format=%H -- web/rounds.json); do
#     git show "$c:web/rounds.json" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"lat"' &&
#       git show "$c:web/rounds.json" | grep -o '"image": *"[^"]*"'
#   done | sed 's/.*\///; s/\.[a-zA-Z0-9]*"$//; s/-[0-9]*$//' | sort -u
